name: Self-Directed Queries Complexity
definition: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}$ be nonempty on a finite domain. For each $S\subseteq X$, a deterministic learner repeatedly chooses an as-yet unqueried $x\in S$, predicts its label, receives the true label of an unknown target $h\in\mathcal H$, and removes $x$ from the remaining set. It must predict every point in $S$. Let $M_{\mathrm{sd}}(\mathcal H,S)$ be the minimum, over such adaptive learners, of the maximum number of incorrect predictions over targets. The **Self-Directed Queries Complexity** is $M_{\mathrm{sd}}(\mathcal H)=\max_{S\subseteq X}M_{\mathrm{sd}}(\mathcal H,S)$; it counts mistakes, not queries. The empty set $S$ has cost zero.
graph_summary: Worst finite-subset self-directed mistake bound: choose each next point adaptively and predict every point once.
origin_references: The self-directed learning model is introduced in \cite{goldman1993learning,goldman1994power}.

monotonic.proof: A self-directed learner with a worst-case mistake bound for all targets in $\mathcal H$ has the same bound when its target is restricted to any subfamily.

c_monotonic.proof: A self-directed strategy for the original class restricts to the fibre after removing fixed coordinates, so its worst-case query count cannot increase.
